seoTitle: How to Insert a Watermark in Google Docs (2026)
metaDescription: Google moved the watermark option in Google Docs to Insert > Page elements. Here's the current path, plus a text (Draft) or logo image watermark and the one document format where it won't work.
intro: If you've gone looking for the watermark option in Google Docs and come up empty, you're not imagining it. Google relocated the feature into a new submenu, so the spot where longtime users expect to find it under Insert no longer shows it directly. This guide covers where it sits now, a fast fallback if you can't find it, and the Watermark panel itself: adding a "DRAFT" text stamp or a logo image, and adjusting its formatting and transparency so it looks intentional instead of like a mistake.
prerequisites: The document must be in pages format, not pageless. Google's own documentation says watermarks aren't available in pageless documents, and any watermark already on the page disappears if you switch to pageless.

steps.heading: Open your document
steps.body: Start from Google Drive with the document you want to watermark. Right-clicking a file gives you the full context menu (Open with, Download, Rename, Share, and more), and selecting it opens the doc in the Docs editor, where the watermark tool lives in the top menu bar, not in Drive itself.

image.caption: Right-clicking a document in Google Drive brings up the full file menu; this is just how you get into the doc before touching the watermark tool itself.

steps.heading: Find Watermark under Insert, Page elements
steps.body: Google moved this option: it now sits under Insert, then Page elements, then Watermark, grouped with header, footer, and other page-level tools instead of listed directly under Insert the way older guides describe. If you'd rather not hunt for it, click Help in the top menu bar and choose Search the menus (or press Option+/), then type "watermark" to jump straight to it no matter which submenu it's currently filed under. That trick works for any Docs feature Google has recently reshuffled, not only this one.

image.caption: The Help menu, with Search the menus at the top; typing what you're looking for here skips hunting through Insert's submenus for a feature Google has moved.

steps.heading: Open the Watermark panel
steps.body: Selecting Watermark opens a side panel on the right with two tabs, Image and Text. The Text tab includes an Insert text field, a Formatting section for font and style, a Transparency slider, and Placement options for Diagonal or Horizontal. Every watermark setting lives in this one panel, so leave it open while you build the watermark in the next step.

image.caption: The Watermark panel with its Image and Text tabs, an empty Insert text field, and controls for formatting, transparency, and diagonal or horizontal placement.

steps.heading: Add and format your text watermark
steps.body: With the Text tab selected, type your watermark text into the Insert text field. "DRAFT" is the classic choice, but any short label works. Pick a font under Formatting (Impact reads as a bold, legible stamp) and drag the Transparency slider toward 0% if you want the text more solid instead of faded into the background. Diagonal placement is selected by default and tends to read most clearly across a full page of text; Horizontal runs the watermark straight across if you'd rather have that.

image.caption: Typing text into the watermark field with Impact formatting applied and transparency pulled down to make the stamp more solid, Diagonal placement selected.

steps.heading: Switch to an image watermark, or remove one
steps.body: Click the Image tab at the top of the same panel instead of Text to stamp a logo. It swaps the field for an upload option where you can select a file from your computer or Drive. The same Transparency and Placement controls carry over, so a logo can be scaled down to something subtle instead of something that competes with the page's actual content. Once a watermark is applied, Remove watermark appears at the bottom of the panel if you want to clear it and start over.

troubleshooting.cause: Google grouped it into a new Page elements submenu instead of leaving it directly under Insert.
troubleshooting.fix: Go to Insert, Page elements, Watermark, or use Help, Search the menus (Option+/) and type watermark to jump straight there.

troubleshooting.problem: Part of the watermark is missing, with visible gaps
troubleshooting.cause: According to Google's own help page, this happens when text behind the watermark has a background color; the watermark is cut where that color sits.
troubleshooting.fix: Remove the background color from the text overlapping the watermark.

troubleshooting.problem: The watermark isn't showing up at all
troubleshooting.cause: The document is in pageless format. Watermarks only render, and only work, in pages format.
troubleshooting.fix: Switch the document back to pages format; the watermark reappears once it's no longer pageless.

faq.question: Why can't I find Insert, Watermark anymore?
faq.answer: Google moved it. The option now lives under Insert, Page elements, Watermark instead of sitting directly under Insert.

faq.question: Is there a faster way to find it if I forget the new path?
faq.answer: Yes. Open Help, choose Search the menus (or press Option+/), and type watermark. It jumps straight to the option no matter which submenu it's filed under.

faq.question: Can I use both a text and image watermark at once?
faq.answer: No. The panel's Image and Text tabs are separate options; applying one replaces the other, so pick whichever type fits the document.

faq.question: Why does my watermark have gaps in it?
faq.answer: Google's own help page attributes this to a background color behind the text on the page. Removing it lets the watermark show in full.

faq.question: Why is the watermark missing entirely?
faq.answer: Check whether the document is in pageless format. Watermarks only display, and only work, when the document is in pages format.

faq.question: How do I remove a watermark once it's added?
faq.answer: Reopen the Watermark panel the same way you found it, and click Remove watermark at the bottom of the panel to clear it.
